Maya (AE): AtlasBank RFP follow-up: they want a 4-week BYOK PoC that demonstrates split-key (threshold) signing with an on-prem HSM cluster and a signed rotation log for auditors. They also asked for a predictable PoC cost.
Victor (AtlasBank): Confirming: we run a prototype where the key is never exportable and signing requires 2-of-3 HSM quorum. Need evidence of non-exportability, attestation, and a rotation playbook. PoC target start in 2 weeks.
Ravi (SE): Two immediate design choices: 1) proxy model where AtlasBank HSM signs on-demand over mTLS, Redwood never holds key material; 2) hybrid where we host a signing gateway in their VPC that talks to the HSM locally. Each has different latency and threat model.
Omar (Security): From our side we need vendor attestation PDFs, HSM firmware versions, and policy that keys are marked non-exportable. Also want to run a signing test vector set to verify deterministic outcomes.
Tina (Infra): Networking for proxy: outbound only from their HSM to our gateway, prefer mutual TLS + short-lived client certs. We'll require an allowlist of our egress IPs and a small NAT pool. For in-VPC gateway we need an IAM role + subnet details.
Sasha (Legal): For PoC we'll use a narrow addendum: data custody, PoC fees, and an acceptance checklist. Also need to confirm whether Redwood is permitted to perform pen-test activity against the PoC environment or if AtlasBank will run the tests.
Ravi (SE): We can produce a deterministic signing test: supply message list and expected signatures (RFC8037 style), then have HSM sign and we validate signature provenance. Example check: `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature sig.bin msg.txt`.
Victor (AtlasBank): Audit team wants signed rotation events that include HSM attestation and chain-of-custody. Can you emit an HSM-signed rotation statement plus an S3-stored audit trail? Retention 7 years for them.
Omar (Security): 7 years is long; default retention is 1 year. We can offer custom retention for enterprise addendum, but we need storage and legal signoff. Also need to document who can trigger rotation and the admin auth flow (MFA, approver list).
Maya (AE): Pricing: they expect a flat PoC price envelope. Suggested: flat engineering + infra reservation for 4 weeks + optional per-100k sign ops above baseline. Victor: is that acceptable?
Victor (AtlasBank): Flat fee helps. Also request a detailed breakdown: setup, runbook, monitoring dashboards, and incident response SLA during PoC.
Tina (Infra): For cutover and rotation tests we'll provide a canary plan: create new key material on HSM, run 10% traffic to new key, validate signatures against test vectors, then full cutover. Caching note: clients will cache public keys for TTL; we'll show how to invalidate caches.
Ravi (SE): Emergency rotate flow: API call -> HSM generates new key shares -> publish rotation event -> optional revocation list push. For threshold HSMs we support coordinate rotate where original shares are zeroed. We can document timing: expect 5-10 minutes for multi-HSM quorum rotate in PoC with tuned network.
Omar (Security): They also demand proof that Redwood cannot reconstruct the key. For proxy model that's okay but we still produce attestation that only signing operations happen and that we never hold key material. Need clear language in addendum.
Sasha (Legal): We'll draft addendum with: statement "Redwood will not have access to key material" for proxy model, audit log delivery, liability cap for PoC, and PoC acceptance criteria. Also note penetration testing: AtlasBank can run tests; Redwood will provide a coordinating contact window.
Maya (AE): Ops ask: Victor, can your infra team provide a small test dataset and a contact for scheduling the outbound tunnel config?
Victor (AtlasBank): Yes 
Contact: ops@atlasbank.internal. We can provide HSM attestation bundle and run the test vectors.
Tina (Infra): Preflight curl example for mTLS handshake and health check:
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy-kms.redwood.example.com:443 -cert client.crt -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://proxy-kms.redwood.example.com/healthz
```
Expect HTTP 200 and JSON `{"status":"ok","hsm_quorum":true}`.
Ravi (SE): PoC acceptance criteria (draft): 1) successful 2-of-3 signing test vector pass, 2) rotation executed and documented, 3) latency within agreed SLO (<50ms median, p99 <350ms), 4) audit logs delivered to Atlas S3.
Victor (AtlasBank): p99 <350ms is aggressive but doable for in-VPC gateway; proxy model will be higher. We'll accept p99 <600ms for proxy model during PoC.
Omar (Security): We'll prepare required attestation list and sample signed rotation statement format.
ci-bot: Created ticket POCCASE-712, assigned to Ravi and Tina.
Maya (AE): Next steps: Ravi + Tina to produce the runbook & test vector package by Thu; Sasha to prepare PoC addendum draft; Omar to list attestation docs. Victor will circulate ops contact and HSM attestation. Aim to kickoff in 2 weeks. :shipit:
_notes: POC discusses threshold HSM, attestation, retention, and pricing envelope
